entries.title: Fixed-length SAW needs an explicit ensemble transfer
entries.statement: A proof for the critical variable-length boundary-to-boundary SAW law does not by itself prove convergence for the uniform n-step honeycomb walk rooted at the origin with a free endpoint. In a fixed finite path collection, conditioning fugacity weights x^L on L=n gives uniform n-step weights, but a shrinking conditioning probability can invalidate transfer from a weak mixture limit. A conditional local limit with relative error, as well as endpoint and domain transfer, is an additional premise. This campaign concept is a draft; it is not an SLE convergence proof.
assumptions: P0003 exact source is Grimmett Question 2.2 (arXiv:2205.07318)
Related chordal source is Duminil-Copin--Smirnov Conjecture 1 (arXiv:1007.0575)

entries.title: Rare prescribed-length conditioning is not determined by a joint weak limit
entries.statement: A weak joint shape/length limit does not determine conditional shape at a prescribed lattice length. For even n, let L_n be uniform on {1/n,2/n,...,1} and let X_n=0 except at L_n=1/2. Choose X_n=+1 there in one sequence and -1 in another. Both joint laws tend to (0,U), where U is uniform on [0,1], and have identical length marginals. Their conditional features at L_n=1/2 are respectively +1 and -1; that atom has mass 1/n. Thus the required transfer must control relative conditional errors, not just a weak mixture limit. Author-derived explicit counterexample; independent review pending.
assumptions: The two finite joint laws are exactly the ones stated
No claim that these laws model actual critical SAW

entries.title: Loewner probe errors require exponent normalization
entries.statement: Small raw drift of derivative-power Loewner probes does not identify a Brownian variance if their positive exponents tend to zero. With deterministic driver W=0 and alpha_n=1/n, on a local interval with bounded derivative jets and h-prime bounded away from zero, (h-prime)^alpha_n tends uniformly to 1. For slit probes (x,s)=(1,1),(-1,1),(1,3), the initial raw relative drifts are alpha_n times (9/8,9/8,33/32), yet the variance rate is zero. At n=128 the maximum raw drift is 9/1024<1/100, while division by alpha_n leaves 9/8. Require a fixed positive common limiting exponent or exponent-normalized error control. Author-derived obstruction; independent review pending.
assumptions: Stop before a Loewner hull meets a probe
The jets and inverse first derivative are locally bounded

entries.title: Relative local limits suffice for fixed-length transfer
entries.statement: A relative local limit is a sufficient fixed-length transfer premise. Let Gamma_delta be curves in a common metric space and let L_delta be an integer length. Suppose Q is a probability law, h_delta>0 tends to zero and rho>0. For every bounded continuous f, assume E[f(Gamma_delta) 1_{L_delta=n_delta}]=h_delta rho Q(f)+o(h_delta), and P(L_delta=n_delta)=h_delta rho+o(h_delta). The conditional laws given L_delta=n_delta then converge weakly to Q, by dividing these asymptotics. This criterion is conditional draft material; its SAW hypotheses are not proved here and independent review is pending.
assumptions: The common curve space is metric
Q is a Borel probability law
The specified relative asymptotics hold for every bounded continuous test function

relations.rationale: The guard says a shrinking length condition can invalidate weak-limit transfer; the rare-atom card exhibits identical weak limits and length marginals with opposite conditional features.
Relative local asymptotics control exactly the selected conditional numerator and denominator that the rare-atom counterexample leaves undetermined.

The ensemble guard needs relative conditioning error; the exponent guard needs error after division by alpha. Both explicitly prevent an absolute error from being used after a vanishing normalization.
The read-only store P0003 statement concerns uniform n-step walks from the honeycomb origin; the guard preserves that exact target when reviewing a related chordal-fugacity argument.
